stages.label: authenticated-candidate
stages.explanation: Three author jobs and one composition prepare the fictional A document/code candidate; no proposed code is executed.

stages.label: quorum-veto-and-three-catalog-edges
stages.explanation: Original A/B approvals and C's objection survive three unrelated D updates; the active objection still blocks acceptance.

stages.label: partial-audit-and-active-author-lease
stages.explanation: The audit is pending after one of three edges. A separate D author lease has token 1 and remains unsubmitted at capture.

stages.label: committed-WAL-state-captured
stages.explanation: A SELECT-only reader remains at revision 1 while ordinary APIs accept revision 2 into WAL; the backup captures revision 2 without changing source events.

stages.label: source-continues-after-capture
stages.explanation: The live source revokes B, completes the audit, submits the original D lease and changes D policy. Historical acceptance replay still returns the same receipt.

stages.label: restored-historical-state-is-readable
stages.explanation: The restored copy preserves receipt, packets, partial checkpoint and the old leased task; B remains historically unrevoked there while the live source has revoked B.

stages.label: restored-writes-and-publish-rejected
stages.explanation: The restored copy rejects acceptance replay, B's old decision, the old lease submit, enqueue and publish before domain changes; publish creates no output directory.

stages.label: quarantine-persists-in-the-database
stages.explanation: Opening the backup DB directly and copying only that marked DB without sidecars both retain the inspection boundary; enqueue is rejected in each copy.

stages.label: safe-operator-rejections
stages.explanation: Missing authority, an existing backup destination, an incomplete empty directory and an existing restore destination are rejected without SQL corruption or overwrites.

limitations: The backup uses SQLite online backup of committed source state while a separate read-only transaction remains at an older revision. No raw live database file is copied.
Private checksums, manifest, schema fingerprints, intent and database files remain outside all public artifacts. Safe inspection summaries report validation outcomes and counts only.
The backup and restored DB are marked inspection-only. Historical grants, leases, approvals and accepted receipts are readable records, not permission to resume writes in a copy.
The marker also survives a copy of only the already-quarantined snapshot DB without filesystem sidecars; no activation operation is provided.
The original source continues independently after capture: revocation, audit advance, D task submission and a later content policy are absent from the captured copy.
Checksums and SQLite integrity/foreign-key checks establish internal file consistency under trust in the implementation and local owner, not external authenticity or semantic truth.
Public snapshot records may disclose the example's public artifact history; bearer files are separate and the private DB still contains credential hashes, so the bundle must remain private.
Configured worker counts and child processes are bounded functional workflow evidence; no throughput, load or service-capacity measurement is made.
The workflow executes no proposed Python, uses no external LLM, performs no SQL corruption and reproduces no process crash or network failure.
Local capability principals establish neither independent people/models nor human understanding, factual truth, inventory completeness or program behavior.
